title: Jacket potatoes & beans
description: The ultimate cheap, cheerful tea.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Scrub and prick 4 large potatoes, then bake on a tray for 50–60 minutes until soft right through.
About 5 minutes before serving, heat the baked beans in a saucepan, stirring until bubbling and hot.
Split each potato, fluff the middle, add beans and, if you want, grated cheese and butter.
safety: Check the middle of each potato is piping hot and soft before serving.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Sausage & bean casserole
description: Big flavour. One pan. Happy plates.
steps: Slice the onion. Brown the sausages in a deep pan for 8–10 minutes, turning; they do not need to be fully cooked yet.
Add the onion, paprika, chopped tomatoes and baked beans. Stir well and nestle the sausages into the sauce.
Cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes until the sausages are completely cooked through and the sauce is bubbling. Serve hot.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: One-pot chicken rice
description: Dinner and minimal washing up.
steps: Dice the boneless chicken thighs into even pieces and chop the onion. Brown both in a large deep pan for 7–8 minutes.

Stir in 300 g dry rice and paprika. Dissolve the stock cube in 650 ml boiling water, pour in, cover and gently simmer for 18–20 minutes. Add a splash more water only if the pan dries out before the rice is tender.
Stir in the frozen peas for the final 4–5 minutes. Check the rice is tender, chicken cooked throughout and the whole pan piping hot. Serve straight away.
safety: Cook chicken thoroughly throughout; check the thickest piece with a clean probe (75°C for 30 seconds, or an equivalent safe time/temperature). Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.

title: Cheat’s cottage pie
description: A cosy classic without the fuss.
steps: Peel and chop the potatoes. Boil for 15–20 minutes until tender, drain and mash.
While they boil, cook the beef mince and diced onion for 8–10 minutes until browned and cooked through. Stir in peas and gravy granules with about 300 ml boiling water; simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Heat the grill. Spoon the beef into an ovenproof dish and spread mashed potato over it; add cheese if using. Grill for 5–8 minutes until golden and piping hot.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Tuna pasta bake
description: The cupboard-clearout hero.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil pasta for 1–2 minutes less than the pack says, then drain.
In a pan over low heat, stir cream cheese with the milk until smooth and warm. Fold in the drained tuna, sweetcorn, pasta and half the grated cheese.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with the remaining cheese and bake for 15–20 minutes until bubbling and piping hot in the middle.
safety: Drain the canned tuna before mixing. Heat the bake until piping hot throughout.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Speedy tomato pasta
description: A very reliable 20-minute dinner.
steps: Put the pasta in a pan of boiling water and cook to the packet time (usually 10–12 minutes).
Meanwhile heat the oil in a frying pan, gently cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add tomatoes and simmer for 10–12 minutes until thickened.
Drain the pasta, toss with the hot sauce and finish with grated cheese.
safety: Serve piping hot; refrigerate any leftovers promptly.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Egg fried rice
description: The quickest fridge raid going.
steps: Cook 300 g dry rice according to the packet (usually 10–12 minutes), drain and use immediately. Alternatively use 900 g cooked rice that was cooled quickly and kept refrigerated for no longer than 24 hours.
Heat a large frying pan, scramble the eggs until set, then stir in the cooked rice and frozen peas. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes, breaking up clumps.
Add soy sauce and chopped spring onions. Stir-fry until everything is steaming hot throughout, then serve immediately.
safety: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.

title: Cheesy bean wraps
description: Crispy, melty, very little effort.
steps: Drain the sweetcorn and warm the beans in a pan until hot. Spoon a little bean mix and grated cheese over half of each wrap.
Fold the wraps. Cook in a dry frying pan in batches for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut each wrap into wedges, checking the filling is hot throughout, and serve.
safety: Keep the filling hot and serve freshly cooked.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Sausage, mash & peas
description: Everyone knows the drill.
steps: Peel and chop potatoes. Put on to boil for 15–20 minutes until completely soft.
While they cook, cook the sausages according to their packet instructions until cooked throughout; boil the frozen peas for 3–4 minutes.
Drain and mash the potatoes, mix gravy granules with hot water following the packet, and serve while everything is hot.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Smoky butter bean stew
description: A cosy dinner from a few tins.
steps: Dice the onion and soften in a saucepan over medium heat with 2 tablespoons water for 5 minutes.
Add paprika, drained butter beans, tomatoes and stock cube dissolved in 150 ml boiling water. Stir.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick, bubbling and hot throughout.
safety: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Chicken & potato traybake
description: Chop, chuck in, oven on.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut potatoes and carrots into 2 cm pieces and slice the onion.
Spread vegetables on a baking tray, toss with oil and roast for 10 minutes. Add evenly sized boneless chicken-thigh pieces and turn everything to coat.
Roast for another 25–35 minutes until the vegetables are soft and chicken is thoroughly cooked in the centre. Do not serve undercooked chicken.
safety: Cook chicken thoroughly throughout; check the thickest piece with a clean probe (75°C for 30 seconds, or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Ham & cheese toasties
description: When cooking feels like too much.
steps: Make four sandwiches with 2 slices of bread, 2 slices of ham and a quarter of the cheese in each. Lightly butter the outside.
Toast in a sandwich maker or frying pan in batches for about 3–4 minutes per side until golden, turning carefully.
Serve when the cheese is fully melted and the filling is hot.
safety: Heat the ham-and-cheese filling until hot; refrigerate any remaining ham promptly.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Meatball spaghetti
description: A dependable midweek winner.
steps: Brown the meatballs in a frying pan for 8–10 minutes, turning. Add the diced onion and cook until softened.
Pour in the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 12–15 minutes, checking the meatballs are completely cooked through.
Meanwhile boil spaghetti/pasta according to the pack. Drain, toss with the meatball sauce and top with grated cheese.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Fish finger butties
description: A five-star lazy tea.
steps: Heat the oven following the fish-finger pack. Bake the fish fingers for the full packet time until cooked through and crisp.
Wash the lettuce and spread the bread with measured mayonnaise.
Divide fish fingers between four sandwiches, add lettuce, close and serve.
safety: Follow the fish-finger cooking instructions; the centre must be cooked and piping hot.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Tomato soup & toasties
description: Easy comfort on a rainy day.
steps: Finely chop the onion. Put it in a saucepan with the tomatoes and stock cube dissolved in 300 ml boiling water; simmer for 15–20 minutes.
Blend the hot soup carefully if you like a smooth texture. Return to the pan and reheat until bubbling.
While soup simmers, make four cheese sandwiches and toast them in a dry frying pan in batches until golden and cheese has melted. Serve together.
safety: Be careful blending hot soup; allow steam to escape and never overfill a sealed blender jug.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Bean chilli jackets
description: A loaded spud without the spend.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and bake the scrubbed potatoes for 50–60 minutes until fully soft inside.
Drain and rinse the kidney beans. Simmer with chopped tomatoes and paprika in a saucepan for 15 minutes, stirring until thick and piping hot.
Split the baked potatoes, spoon over the bean chilli and finish with cheese.
safety: Use canned kidney beans; do not substitute uncooked dried kidney beans without properly boiling and preparing them.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Sausage & potato traybake
description: All on one tray, nothing fancy.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Chop potatoes and carrots into 2 cm chunks and slice the onion. Toss vegetables with oil on a large tray.
Roast the vegetables for 15 minutes, then add the sausages, turning to coat.
Roast for 25–30 minutes more, turning sausages once, until potatoes are tender and sausages cooked all the way through.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Cheat’s chicken pie
description: A cosy pie with a ready-made lid.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Dice chicken thighs and carrots. Cook chicken in a large frying pan for 8–10 minutes until nearly cooked; add carrots and peas.
Mix gravy granules with 300 ml boiling water. Pour into the pan and simmer for 5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the filling is thick.
Spoon into a baking dish, lay the ready-rolled pastry over the top and cut a small steam hole. Bake for 20–25 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling piping hot.
safety: Cook chicken thoroughly throughout; check the thickest piece with a clean probe (75°C for 30 seconds, or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Tuna & sweetcorn jackets
description: Cheap potatoes with a filling that works.
steps: Heat oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Scrub, prick and bake the potatoes for 50–60 minutes until fully soft inside.
Drain the tuna and sweetcorn thoroughly, then mix with mayonnaise in a bowl. Keep refrigerated until serving.
Split the hot potatoes and divide the cold tuna filling between them. Serve straight away.
safety: Keep tuna mayonnaise chilled until needed; do not leave it at room temperature while potatoes bake.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Creamy chicken & pea rice
description: One pot and proper comfort food.
steps: Dice chicken and onion. Brown both in a large deep pan for about 8 minutes.
Add dry rice and a stock cube dissolved in 650 ml boiling water. Cover and simmer gently for 18–20 minutes, topping up with a splash of water only if needed.
Add frozen peas for the last 5 minutes. Stir through cream cheese, heat until bubbling and check the chicken is completely cooked and the rice tender. Serve straight away.
safety: Cook chicken thoroughly throughout; check the thickest piece with a clean probe (75°C for 30 seconds, or an equivalent safe time/temperature). Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.

title: Creamy broccoli pasta
description: Four ingredients. Creamy without a faff.
steps: Boil pasta in plenty of water according to the pack. Add small broccoli florets for the final 4–5 minutes until tender.
Before draining, scoop out 150 ml of pasta water. Drain the pasta and broccoli.
Gently warm cream cheese and crushed garlic in the pan with enough reserved pasta water to make a coating sauce. Fold in pasta and broccoli, heat through and serve.
safety: Wash fresh broccoli and heat the sauce thoroughly before serving.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Smoky bean rice bowls
description: More tins, less spending.
steps: Cook the dry rice according to its packet, usually 10–12 minutes. Drain and serve straight away.
Meanwhile finely chop the onion and soften in a frying pan with 2 tablespoons water for 5 minutes.
Add drained canned kidney beans, chopped tomatoes and paprika. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until thick and steaming hot; spoon over rice.
safety: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.

title: Chicken salad wraps
description: A midweek wrap with proper dinner filling.
steps: Cut boneless chicken thighs into thin, even strips. Toss with paprika and fry in a non-stick pan, turning, for 12–15 minutes until cooked throughout.
Wash and shred the lettuce, grate carrots and warm wraps briefly according to the pack.
Spread the wraps with mayonnaise, divide the hot chicken and vegetables between them, roll tightly and serve immediately.
safety: Cook chicken thoroughly throughout; check the thickest piece with a clean probe (75°C for 30 seconds, or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: One-pot sausage pasta
description: A pan of tomato pasta that fills everyone up.
steps: Slice sausages into bite-sized pieces and brown in a deep non-stick pan for 8–10 minutes, turning to colour.
Add diced onion, chopped tomatoes, paprika and 500 ml boiling water. Stir in dry pasta, cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes, stirring often and adding water if needed.
Check the pasta is tender, sauce thick and every sausage piece cooked through before serving.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature).
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Cheesy vegetable wraps
description: A cupboard-and-freezer dinner.
steps: Simmer frozen peas for 3–4 minutes until hot, then drain well. Drain the sweetcorn.
Mix peas, sweetcorn, grated cheese and paprika. Divide among 8 wraps and fold the wraps closed.
Toast in batches in a dry frying pan for 2–3 minutes each side until crisp, cheese melted and filling piping hot.
safety: Make sure the frozen peas are thoroughly heated before filling the wraps.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Egg & pea noodles
description: A fast, filling noodle bowl.
steps: Cook noodles according to the packet. Add frozen peas for the final 3 minutes, then drain well.
Beat eggs and scramble in a non-stick frying pan until set. Add drained noodles and peas.
Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes until everything is piping hot. Stir in soy sauce and sliced spring onions and serve.
safety: Cook eggs until set and the noodle mixture piping hot; leftovers should be chilled promptly.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Fish fingers & homemade wedges
description: Crisp potatoes and no fuss.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut potatoes into slim wedges and toss with oil on a tray.
Roast wedges for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway. Cook fish fingers on a separate tray for the time and temperature stated on their pack so they finish together.
Boil the frozen peas for 3–4 minutes until hot. Serve wedges, fish fingers and peas together, checking everything is cooked.
safety: Follow the fish-finger packet instructions and serve only once cooked through.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Easy beef & bean chilli
description: One big pan, plenty of leftovers.
steps: Dice onion and brown with the beef mince in a large pan for 8–10 minutes, stirring until the mince is cooked through.
Drain canned kidney beans and add to the pan with chopped tomatoes and paprika. Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes until bubbling and thick.
Meanwhile cook dry rice according to the packet, drain and serve the hot chilli on top.
safety: Cook raw chicken, sausages and mince thoroughly throughout. If checking with a clean food probe, the centre should reach at least 75°C for 30 seconds (or an equivalent safe time/temperature). Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.

title: Red lentil & tomato soup
description: A cheap, hearty bowl from the cupboard.
steps: Rinse red lentils until the water runs clearer. Dice the onion and carrots.
Put lentils, vegetables, tomatoes and a stock cube dissolved in 900 ml boiling water into a large pan.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft and soup thick. Add a little water if needed and serve piping hot.
safety: Cook lentils fully until softened; cool leftover soup promptly and reheat thoroughly.
storage: Cool leftovers and put in the fridge within two hours. Eat within 48 hours or freeze; reheat only once until steaming hot throughout.

title: Chickpea & spinach curry
description: A gentle, budget-friendly curry.
steps: Cook dry rice according to its packet and set aside for immediate serving.
Meanwhile drain canned chickpeas. Add them to a pan with chopped tomatoes, curry powder and frozen spinach.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring until spinach is fully thawed and everything piping hot. Serve with freshly cooked rice.
safety: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
storage: Serve straight away. Cool any leftover rice quickly, ideally within one hour, refrigerate, eat within 24 hours and reheat only once until steaming hot.
